title: In-situ analysis and monitoring of antiscalant polyaspartate by mobile fluorescence spectroscopy
author: Pettauer, Leis, et al.

steps.title: Prepare PASP solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve each of the three commercially available PASP products in both groundwater and pure Merck Milli‑Q Type 1 water to obtain test solutions.

steps.title: Generate calibration curves
steps.instruction: Prepare a series of PASP standards covering the expected concentration range, measure their fluorescence (see step 7) and plot intensity versus concentration to obtain calibration curves.

steps.title: Evaluate pH effect
steps.instruction: Adjust the pH of separate PASP solutions to the desired values and record fluorescence at each pH to assess the influence on the signal.

steps.title: Assess temperature effect
steps.instruction: Conduct fluorescence measurements of PASP solutions at a controlled temperature of 20 ± 1 °C; additionally evaluate the temperature dependence by measuring at temperatures from 5 °C to 30 °C.

steps.title: Test turbidity/adsorption
steps.instruction: Add calcite (CaCO₃) and bentonite powder to separate PASP solutions to investigate turbidity and adsorption effects on fluorescence.

steps.title: Configure spectrofluorometer
steps.instruction: Set up the Jasco FP‑6500 spectrofluorometer with a standard quartz cuvette; select the synchronous scan technique in constant‑wavelength mode with a wavelength offset of 100 nm between excitation and emission.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence
steps.instruction: Record the synchronous fluorescence spectrum of each PASP sample; the characteristic PASP peak should appear near 415 nm.

steps.title: Convert intensity to concentration
steps.instruction: Use the calibration curves to convert measured fluorescence intensities to PASP concentrations.

steps.title: Note detection limits
steps.instruction: Recognize that the detection limit for PASP with this method is 0.15 mg L⁻¹ and the measurement uncertainty (1 σ) is approximately ±0.1 mg L⁻¹.

steps.title: Represent data uncertainty
steps.instruction: When plotting calibration curves or other results, display error bars corresponding to a 2 σ confidence interval (95.4 %).
